div.head: II Cn 22.1
div.ab: And ungetrywan men ceose man anfealdne að on þrim hundredum, ⁊ þryfealdne að, swa wide swa hit to ðære byrig hyre; oððon ga to þam ordale.
⁊ ungetrewe menn ceose man anfealdre að on þrim hundrede, ⁊ þryfealdne að, swa wide swa hyt to þare byrig hyre; oððe to þam ordale.
Incredibili eligatur simplex láda in tribus hundretis, et triplex iuramentum tam late, sicut ad ipsam curiam obeditur; uel eat ad ordalium.
And ungetreowan men ceose man anfealdne að on þreom hundredan ⁊ þreofealdne að swa wíde swa hit to ðære byrig hyre, oððe gá to ordale.
And ungetrywan men ceose man anfealdne að on þrim hundredum; and þryfealdne að, swa wide swa hit to ðære byrig hyre; oððon ga to þam ordale.

Und einem unglaubwürdigen Manne erwähle man [das Gericht] einfachen Eid [durch] in drei [dieser und zwei nachbarlichen] Hundertschaften [ansässige] Helfer und [wenn das Urtheil lautet auf] dreifachen Eid, [Helfer aus dem Gebiete,] so weit wie das zu dieser Gerichtsstadt gehört; oder jener schreite zum Ordal.

And for an untrustworthy man let [the court] choose the single oath [with helpers resident] in three hundreds [this and two neighbouring ones], and [if the judgment is for] the threefold oath, [helpers from the area] as far as belongs to that borough; or let him go to the ordeal.

And for an untrustworthy man compurgators for the simple oath shall be selected within three hundreds, and for the triple oath, throughout the district under the jurisdiction of the borough-court; otherwise he shall go to the ordeal.
And for an untrustworthy man one is to select a simple oath within three hundreds, and a three-fold oath from the area which belongs to the borough; or he is to go to the ordeal.

And guarantors for the simple oath of the untrustworthy man shall be chosen from the three hundreds; and for the threefold oath, from throughout the jurisdiction of the borough court; otherwise he must undergo the ordeal.
div.note: A's ‘anfealdre’ should be ‘-dne’; A should supply ‘ga’ before ‘to þam ordale’. In B, ‘on þreom hundredan ⁊ þreofealdne að’ was added in the 16th century in the margin.
This means that he is not allowed to choose his own compurgators, but the court appoints them, according to whether the case demands a simple or three-fold oath.
to þam ordale: to ordale B
